about.title: About
about.p1: It all started with a curiosity: understanding how things work behind the screen. That curiosity became a discipline, then a direction.
about.p2: Today I'm learning web development methodically — every project is a mission, every bug an anomaly to resolve, every deployment a small launch.
about.p3: My vision: building web experiences that are as enjoyable to use as they are to craft.
skills.title: Skills
missions.title: Mission logs
missions.m1.name: Xibaar Yi
missions.m1.desc: “The news” in Wolof: a Senegalese news site in PHP and MySQL, with no framework. Real headlines from Senegalese media arrive automatically via RSS, comments are moderated, and a back-office handles roles. Sessions, CSRF protection, image uploads: I wrote it all by hand to understand what frameworks do. A team project at ESP that I have maintained and hardened since.
missions.m1.shot: Xibaar Yi home page: latest articles, news briefs and most-read stories
missions.m1.shot2: A Xibaar Yi article page, with breadcrumbs and a “Read also” column
missions.m1.shot3: Xibaar Yi back office: article management table with search, category filter and actions
missions.m1.shot4: Xibaar Yi back office: comment moderation with pending, approved and spam comments
missions.m2.name: Academic manager
missions.m2.desc: A C program to manage students' grades and subjects. An algorithms team project built at ESP: data structures and logic written end to end in C.
missions.m3.name: Le Voyage Observé
missions.m3.desc: This portfolio, the one you are exploring right now. Framework-free JavaScript, a starry sky drawn in Canvas, GSAP animations synced to scrolling, and two languages. It respects accessibility settings: reduced motion, keyboard navigation and screen readers, and stays readable without JavaScript.
missions.m4.name: Énora Cosmetics
missions.m4.desc: A real online body-care shop, delivering in Dakar. Next.js and TypeScript for the site, Supabase for the database, accounts and photos. Checkout fits on one page (cash on delivery, Wave, Orange Money or WhatsApp): the total, stock and promo code are checked in the database in a single transaction. A back office handles orders, stock, products, reviews and articles. Access is locked down table by table (RLS), with Vitest and Playwright tests.
missions.m4.shot: Énora Cosmetics home page: “Body care, with elegance”, featuring Dove soaps
missions.m4.shot2: Énora Cosmetics shop: category and scent filters, sorting and a product grid
missions.m4.shot3: Énora Cosmetics product page: photo, price in FCFA, quantity and “Add to cart” button
missions.m4.shot4: An Énora journal article: an illustrated beauty tip with its publication date
journey.title: Journey
journey.j1.d: First line of code. Discovering HTML and CSS — and the urge to build.
journey.j2.d: Structured JavaScript learning. First personal projects, first GitHub repositories.
journey.j3.d: Building this portfolio: animation, accessibility, performance. The laboratory of everything I'm learning.
journey.j5.d: Énora Cosmetics, an online shop in production: React with Next.js, TypeScript and Supabase, from the catalogue to the back office.
journey.j4.d: Going further with React, TypeScript and the backend. Goal: joining a team and contributing to real-world projects.

planet.neptune.f2: Its winds are the fastest in the solar system: over 2,000 km/h.

planet.sun.f2: Thanks for making the trip all the way here. Shall we write what comes next?
